holidays.name: National Brisket Day
holidays.description: A day for smoky, slow-cooked, melt-in-your-mouth beef brisket. Pitmasters, home cooks and barbecue fans all get a reason to fire up the smoker or braise a big cut of meat for hours.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance with no single known founder. Brisket has deep roots in Jewish cooking, where it was braised for holidays and family meals. It later became a barbecue legend in Texas, where it is usually smoked low and slow.
holidays.funFact: Brisket comes from the tough chest muscle of the cow, which works hard all day. That is why it needs hours of slow cooking to turn tender.

holidays.name: National Hamburger Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble patty-on-a-bun, which closes out National Burger Month and kicks off grilling season. Expect toppings, backyard cookouts and plenty of debate over cheese, pickles and the best bun.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that is widely observed in the U.S. on May 28. The hamburger is named after Hamburg, Germany, and became an American favorite. It was famously popularized at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair.
holidays.funFact: The hamburger has no ham in it. Its name comes from the German city of Hamburg.

holidays.name: Whooping Crane Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate North America's tallest bird, a elegant white crane with a loud, trumpeting call. It is also meant to raise awareness about protecting this endangered species and its wetland homes.
holidays.origin: This is an observance dedicated to conservation awareness for the whooping crane. The species was reduced to roughly 20 birds in the 1940s, and decades of protection and breeding efforts have helped it recover somewhat.
holidays.funFact: Whooping cranes stand about five feet tall. Their calls can carry for miles.
